blockers.quote: The band came with a leaflet. It sets out the deal.
blockers.why: Check #16 fails: the rule runs through lines 86–100 instead of two or three lines, and the limit is not explicitly flagged.
blockers.fix: Replace lines 86–100 with three spoken lines: “The band came with a leaflet: wear it to bed, and the company runs its work on your brain and pays by the hour. / One company can link many bands, for one big job. But the leaflet promises each brain stays separate. One brain, one band, one jar. / You remember nothing except crumbs—a taste, a word, a face that isn't yours. It calls them harmless. Remember that.”

blockers.quote: And you're not the only one counting. The nurse has a band under her cap now, so the clinic shuts at noon. Therefore your boss sees the jar on your desk, and opens a nap room at work. With a till.
blockers.why: Check #5 fails: the clinic closing does not cause the boss to see the jar, so “therefore” disguises an “and then” transition.
blockers.fix: “The nurse has a band under her cap now, so the clinic shuts at noon. You take the jar back to work; your boss sees it and opens a nap room. With a till.”

blockers.quote: Ninety dollars. For eight hours of lying down. The best wage of your life. And that's the problem.
blockers.why: Check #6 fails on the first full use: you expect the promised payment and receive exactly that, with no gap.
blockers.fix: “Ninety dollars. For eight hours of lying down. Plus a taste in your mouth from a meal you've never eaten. The best wage of your life. And that's the problem.”

suggestions.quote: Morning four. You fold a fitted sheet into a perfect square. Nobody can fold a fitted sheet. His spoon hits the floor.
suggestions.fix: Beat the familiar fitted-sheet gag: have him unfold it, fail to refold it, and hide the resulting ball under his cap before asking, “Since when can you do that?”

suggestions.quote: Therefore the grandmother next door, eleven hours a night, out-earns the whole street.
suggestions.fix: Remove the forced connector: “Eleven hours makes the grandmother next door the street's top earner.”

suggestions.quote: An eighteenth-century chess robot had a chess master hidden inside it (c17). Amazon named a website after it, Mechanical Turk, and paid people a few cents a task (c17). This is the human inside the machine. In bulk.
suggestions.fix: Tighten the analogy onto the picture: “That old chess robot hid a chess master inside it (c17). The warehouse is the same trick: the machine is a thousand people who need twelve dollars.”

keep.quote: Sign, and nobody in this house sits in that chair again. Don't, and it's Thursday forever. You can't sleep on it. Sleeping is the job.
The biggest idea people ever had together, and nobody was awake for it.
